answer.origin: Motley Fool article by Robert Izquierdo, published 2026-08-01 (fool.com coverage 'Nvidia vs. Alphabet'); it cites company filings as its data source, with data as of July 31, 2026. No primary filing is linked in the supplied record.
answer.note: Material source claims concerning NVDA: (1) The article reports that Nvidia's most recent quarter (period ended April 2026) had revenue of $81.6 billion and that the company forecast revenue of $91 billion for the next quarter, with its Vera Rubin AI platform expected to contribute to continued growth. This is a secondhand guidance figure, so its strength depends on confirming it against Nvidia's own release or filing. (2) The article states Alphabet is among Nvidia's customers, but gives no purchase amount, period or product. (3) Alphabet's Google Cloud Q2 2026 revenue was $24.8 billion, up 82% year over year, with backlog above $500 billion, up from $462 billion in Q1. This is an Alphabet result, not an Nvidia figure. It can inform AI demand conditions at a customer of Nvidia, but it does not show that Google Cloud's growth comes from Nvidia hardware. Conditional interpretation: if the $91 billion guidance is confirmed, it supports continued near-term revenue growth expectations for NVDA. The Alphabet customer link is a demand-side hypothesis only; it is not a confirmed purchase relationship and does not establish any Nvidia revenue from Google Cloud. The Google Cloud growth may reflect Alphabet's own accelerators or other infrastructure, which the article does not address.
limitations: The $91 billion next-quarter Nvidia revenue figure is a forecast reported by a third-party article; no primary Nvidia source is supplied to confirm it or its basis.
The article gives no dollar amount, period, or product for Alphabet's purchases from Nvidia, so the size of this customer relationship is unknown.

The unlabeled revenue table mixes both companies' quarterly figures without attribution, so the $119.8 billion (period ended June 2026) figure cannot be reliably assigned to either company from this record.
Google Cloud's growth and backlog do not disclose the share, if any, supplied by Nvidia; the link from Alphabet cloud demand to Nvidia revenue is unestablished.
No historical records or comparison sources were supplied, so the article's claims cannot be checked against prior reported figures for either company.
follow_up: Retrieve Nvidia's most recent quarterly earnings release and outlook (quarter ended April 26, 2026) to confirm the $81.6 billion revenue figure and the $91 billion next-quarter guidance, including whether it is a point or range.
Check Nvidia's annual and quarterly filings for any disclosed customer concentration or named customers that would indicate Alphabet's purchase amount, if disclosed.

Check Alphabet's Q2 2026 earnings release to confirm the Google Cloud revenue ($24.8 billion), growth rate (82%), and backlog figures, and whether Alphabet discloses its accelerator or hardware suppliers.
Verify the attribution of the unlabeled table entries to each company using each company's filing period definitions.
